This is a draft for checking only. It is not a bill of lading or an air waybill and cannot be used to ship, claim or release cargo. Only the carrier, NVOCC or airline (or its agent) issues the real document and its number.
Is this a real bill of lading or air waybill?

No. It is a draft for checking only and is marked DRAFT on every page. Only the shipping line, NVOCC or airline (or its agent) issues the real document and its number. Use this to agree the details with your forwarder and buyer before that happens.
Why make a draft at all?

Most B/L amendments and air waybill corrections come from small typing errors: a wrong consignee address, a missing HS code, a container number with one digit out. Sending your forwarder a clean draft first saves amendment fees and delays at destination.
How does it check container and AWB numbers?

Container numbers are checked against the ISO 6346 check digit. Air waybill numbers are checked with the IATA rule: the first 7 digits of the serial divided by 7 must leave the last digit as the remainder.
How is the chargeable weight worked out?

For each line we take the higher of the gross weight and the volume weight (length × width × height in cm ÷ 6000), rounded up to the next half kilo. Your airline or forwarder may use a different factor, so check their rate sheet.
